text.en:
Currency Act 1967
Currency
(Denominations and Characteristics of Coins)
Notification 2025
Pursuant to section 17(5) of the Currency Act 1967, it is notified for general information that the denominations and characteristics of the coins to be issued on 1 January 2026 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore are as shown in the Schedule.

THE SCHEDULE
DESCRIPTION OF THE 2026 CHINESE ALMANAC COINS
(YEAR OF THE HORSE) TO BE ISSUED ON 1 JANUARY 2026
Part 1
Denomination
$2
Metal
999 Fine Silver
Nickel‑plated 99% Zinc
Standard Weight
7.776 g + 0.15 g
20.000 g + 1.70 g
Standard Diameter
27.00 mm ± 0.30 mm
40.70 mm ± 0.40 mm
Standard Thickness
1.90 mm ± 0.40 mm
2.90 mm ± 0.40 mm
Shape
Round
Edge
Milled
Design of Obverse
1.The background of the $2 silver proof‑like colour coin and the $2 nickel‑plated zinc proof‑like coin is shiny silver.
2.The Singapore Coat of Arms is engraved in the centre of the coin with the year‑date “2026” below it.
3.The word “SINGAPORE” appears once in each of the 4 official languages and is engraved on the coin around the Singapore Coat of Arms.
Design of Reverse
1.The background of the $2 silver proof‑like colour coin and the $2 nickel‑plated zinc proof‑like coin is shiny silver.
2.The $2 silver proof‑like colour coin and the $2 nickel‑plated zinc proof‑like coin share a common design which features —
(a)a horse in a rearing position in the centre of the foreground and on the Kelong Bridge at the Punggol Waterway, with its forelegs, head and tail partially covering the stilt‑like posts of the Kelong Bridge;
(b)the Jewel Bridge in the background on the left side of the coin;
(c)trees in the background on the left and right sides of the coin; and
(d)the denomination “$2” engraved and placed at 7 o’clock, below the horse.
3.The weight in troy oz and fineness of the coin are engraved above the horse of the $2 silver proof‑like colour coin.
4.The horse featured in the $2 silver proof‑like colour coin is in colour.

Design of Obverse
1.The background of the $5 silver proof coin and the $5 silver proof colour coin is shiny silver.
2.The background of the $5 gold brilliant uncirculated coin is shiny gold.
3.The Singapore Coat of Arms is engraved in the centre of the coin with the year‑date “2026” below it.
4.The word “SINGAPORE” appears once in each of the 4 official languages and is engraved on the coin around the Singapore Coat of Arms.
5.The mintmark is engraved on the coin around the Singapore Coat of Arms at 5 o’clock for the $5 silver proof coin and the $5 silver proof colour coin.
Design of Reverse
1.The background of the $5 silver proof coin and the $5 silver proof colour coin is shiny silver.
2.The background of the $5 gold brilliant uncirculated coin is shiny gold.
3.The $5 silver proof coin and the $5 silver proof colour coin share a common design which features —
(a)a horse in a rearing position in the centre of the foreground and on the Kelong Bridge at the Punggol Waterway, with its forelegs, head and tail partially covering the stilt‑like posts of the Kelong Bridge;
(b)the Jewel Bridge in the background on the left side of the coin;
(c)trees in the background on the left and right sides of the coin;
(d)the denomination “$5” engraved and placed at 7 o’clock, below the horse; and
(e)the weight in troy oz and fineness of the coin, engraved above the horse.
4.The horse featured in the $5 silver proof colour coin is in colour.
5.The $5 gold brilliant uncirculated coin features —
(a)a horse engraved in the centre;
(b)the denomination “$5” engraved and placed at 6 o’clock, below the horse; and
(c)the weight in grams and fineness of the coin, engraved above the horse.
